classification.difficultyReason: Uses explicitly prompted intercepts, completing the square, substitution and subtraction, then interprets the vertex of the supplied distance quadratic; the intermediate parts scaffold the modelling decisions.

content.prompt: Gipps Road and Bells Road are two non-intersecting roads in the country. The government wishes to build a road running North–South that connects these two roads. They employ you to work out where to build this connecting road in order to minimise its length. The path of Gipps Road is given by the equation $y=x^2-4x+9$, while the path of Bells Road is given by the equation $y=2x-2$. In this model the positive direction of the $x$-axis runs due East while the positive direction of the $y$-axis runs due North. All lengths are in kilometres.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch a graph of Bells Road. Clearly mark in the $x$- and $y$-intercepts.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=2(0)-2\\y&=-2\end{align*}$$
The $y$-intercept is $(0,-2)$.
$$\begin{align*}0&=2x-2\\2x&=2\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
The $x$-intercept is $(1,0)$. Draw the straight line through these points.

spec.description: Answer-only intercept sketch of Bells Road; no grid or extra ticks.

children.label: i
children.prompt: By completing the square, write the equation for Gipps Road in the form $y=(x-h)^2+k$.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: What will be the $y$-value for Gipps Road when $x=0$?

children.label: iii
children.prompt: Hence, on the same set of axes used to sketch Bells Road, sketch the graph for the path of Gipps Road. Clearly label the turning point and $y$-intercept.

answer.short: Upward-opening parabola with turning point $(2,5)$ and $y$-intercept $(0,9)$, on the axes from part a.
answer.worked: From $y=(x-2)^2+5$, the turning point is $(2,5)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=2$. The parabola opens upwards and passes through $(0,9)$ and its reflection $(4,9)$. Add this curve to the axes from part a.

spec.description: Both roads on one set of axes, with required intercepts and turning point.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the distance between the two points on the roads where $x=0$.

answer.worked:
The points are $(0,9)$ and $(0,-2)$, so their North–South distance is
$$\begin{align*}d&=9-(-2)\\d&=11\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: When $x=a$, find, in terms of $a$, the $y$-value of:

children.label: e
children.prompt: Hence, show that the North–South distance, $d$ km, between the two roads when $x=a$ is given by $d=a^2-6a+11$.

answer.worked:
Subtract the $y$-value of Bells Road from that of Gipps Road:
$$\begin{align*}d&=(a^2-4a+9)-(2a-2)\\d&=a^2-4a+9-2a+2\\d&=a^2-6a+11.\end{align*}$$
This is positive because $a^2-6a+11=(a-3)^2+2$, so Gipps Road is always north of Bells Road.

children.label: f
children.prompt: On a new set of axes, sketch a graph of $d$ against $a$. Clearly label the turning point.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}d&=a^2-6a+11\\d&=(a^2-6a+3^2)+11-3^2\\d&=(a-3)^2+2\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(3,2)$, the axis of symmetry is $a=3$, and the vertical intercept is $(0,11)$. The parabola opens upwards and has no horizontal intercepts.

spec.description: Separate distance-against-position graph with turning point and vertical intercept.

children.label: g
children.prompt: Hence, report back to the government on how long and how far East of the origin the North–South connection road should be built in order to minimise its length.

answer.short:
Build a $2\text{ km}$ North–South road $3\text{ km}$ east of the origin.

The minimum follows from the turning point $(3,2)$ of the distance graph.
answer.worked: Since $d=(a-3)^2+2$ and $(a-3)^2\geq0$, the minimum distance is $2\text{ km}$ at $a=3$. The government should build the North–South connection road $3\text{ km}$ east of the origin, with length $2\text{ km}$.
